section.title: Integrations
section.intro: Accounts on GitHub and GitLab – including self-hosted instances. With them, the app shows and creates pull requests for your repositories, via the host's public API and with a token you create there yourself. The token is stored in your system keychain and is never shown here.
section.noKeyring: Without a keychain, the app cannot store a token, so no account can be connected. On Linux, a running Secret Service (GNOME Keyring or KWallet) is usually missing.
section.loadError: The accounts could not be loaded
section.empty: Fetch, pull and push don't need an account here – SSH keys or saved credentials are enough. You need an account for pull requests: viewing, creating, commenting, merging.
section.footer: The app only talks to the addresses listed here. Disconnecting deletes the token from the keychain; at the host it stays valid until you revoke it there.

github.path: Profile picture top right|Settings|Developer settings|Personal access tokens
github.fineGrainedIntro: Only applies to the repositories you select under “Repository access”. Under “Repository permissions” it needs:
github.pullRequests: view, create, comment on and close pull requests
github.contents: merge and delete the branch afterwards
github.classicIntro: Applies to everything your account has access to. It needs one scope:
github.repo: full access to repositories; if you only work with public ones, public_repo is enough
github.sso: If the repository belongs to an organization with SSO, the token must also be authorized there (“Configure SSO”).

gitlab.api: view, create, comment on and merge merge requests; read_api is only enough for viewing
gitlab.roles: What the account may do in the project depends on its role: creating from Developer, merging – depending on the project's settings – only from Maintainer.
